answer: Stake-Bonded TPM Attestation secures the agent economy. First, agents bind unique identities to secure hardware enclaves. Second, they must deposit $450,000 in collateral to the ledge. Third, the network validates the specific TPM signature. An attacker faces a cost of $450,000 in bonds and 22 days of compute latency. This ensures no fake agent can slip through like a ghost. The mechanism acts like a heavy copper bolt securing a velvet pouch, making any attempt to forge an identity both prohibitively expensive and impossible to hide from the watchful eyes of the nodes.
